stories.title: Mamdani Faces Accountability Assembly on Housing and NYCHA Repairs
stories.dek: Mayor Zohran Mamdani met with clergy and community leaders at Queens College to review campaign promises on housing, public safety and NYCHA repairs.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani appeared Sunday at an accountability assembly at Queens College, where clergy and community leaders organized by the nonpartisan coalition Metro IAF reviewed promises he made during his campaign, NY1 reported.

Organizers said the event was meant to measure his progress on commitments made a year earlier, when he met with the group as a candidate. The coalition focused on four areas: community safety, the mental health crisis, public housing and affordable housing, according to NY1.

Mamdani received a standing ovation and pledged to work with the coalition to maximize density and build thousands of affordable homes on city-owned land at the shuttered Aqueduct Race Track site in South Ozone Park, Queens, NY1 reported. He said the group had told him it could not afford to wait for what the city plans to build.

Joseph Smith, an East New York resident, told NY1 that more affordable housing would help people being priced out of the city. Blanca Ramos, a NYCHA resident from the Lower East Side, said she was encouraged by plans to expand NYCHA's Critical Repairs Initiative citywide to speed urgent maintenance, with a June 30 target for implementation.

The commitments remain pledges. NY1 reported no unit count, construction timeline or confirmed funding for the Aqueduct site. Metro IAF leaders said they plan to keep an open line of communication with the mayor to ensure he follows through.

sources.title: Mamdani faces accountability assembly on housing, NYCHA repairs

stories.title: Videos Show Marble Hill ICE Shooting Unfolded in Seconds
stories.dek: Footage of the Oct. 8 shooting in Marble Hill shows a brief, chaotic encounter, while federal officials say officers believed they were in danger.
body: Video of the Oct. 8 shooting by immigration officers in Marble Hill shows the encounter unfolded in a few chaotic seconds, according to an Associated Press report published by NY1. A 28-year-old Dominican man driving with his 5-year-old son was wounded; the child was not hurt.

One NYPD camera video shows two plainclothes officers running to the car with guns drawn, one striking a window with his gun before the driver sped away, the AP reported. A second video shows people diving for cover as the car stopped against a concrete barrier with bullet holes in the windshield and a rear window. The footage did not show whether the shooting was justified.

Marcos Charles, head of ICE enforcement and removal operations, said the driver refused orders, accelerated and hit two government vehicles, and that officers believed their lives were in danger. He called the neck wound superficial. Senior officials said officers did not know the child was in the car. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin blamed the driver for putting his son at risk.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said federal officers fired seven rounds, according to the AP. Mayor Zohran Mamdani called the shooting an outrage, and he and Gov. Kathy Hochul said they unsuccessfully pressed Mullin and President Trump for the man's release and urged release of ICE body camera footage. Mullin said the footage would be released but did not say when.

The man's lawyers say he is being held in a federal jail in Brooklyn with a bullet still in his body. A judge temporarily barred the government from removing him, and Bronx District Attorney Darcel Clark said her office is investigating.

sources.title: Videos show ICE shooting in NYC unfolded in a few chaotic seconds

stories.title: Mamdani Orders NYPD Use-of-Force Review After Officer Retires Before Trial
stories.dek: The mayor ordered a review of police use-of-force policies after an officer in a fatal 2024 Queens shooting retired before facing a disciplinary trial.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered a comprehensive review of NYPD use-of-force policies and new accountability measures after an officer involved in the fatal 2024 police shooting of a 19-year-old in Ozone Park, Queens, retired before his disciplinary trial, amNY reported.

City Hall said the review, led by Chief of Department Michael LiPetri and Deputy Commissioner Michael Gerber, is the first of its kind in a decade and will include community input, according to amNY. The administration is adding $2.6 million to the NYPD Office of the Inspector General, which City Hall said would triple its headcount.

The NYPD admitted it failed to notify the Civilian Complaint Review Board that Officer Salvatore Alongi was seeking retirement, amNY reported. He retired in May with an accidental disability pension, and the CCRB confirmed he will not face a departmental trial. Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch apologized and called it human error; the department said a civilian employee was demoted and reassigned.

Under new procedures, retirement applications tied to pending CCRB cases will get two levels of review, and officers who retire with pending charges will be reported to the state, which can lead to decertification, according to amNY. Police union leaders criticized the review, while the young man's parents rejected the human-error explanation and called for Tisch's firing.
The state attorney general declined criminal charges in December 2025. A CCRB disciplinary trial for the second officer, Matthew Cianfrocco, will proceed, with no date set, amNY reported.

sources.title: Mamdani orders NYPD use-of-force review, accountability reforms as officer in Win Rozario shooting avoids disciplinary trial through retirement

stories.title: Marble Hill Detainee Still Has Bullet in His Neck, Attorneys Say
stories.dek: Lawyers for the man shot by an ICE agent in Marble Hill say he remains in federal custody in Brooklyn without needed surgery.
body: The man shot by an ICE agent in Marble Hill on Oct. 8 still has a bullet lodged in his neck and has not eaten since being taken into custody, his attorneys from the Legal Aid Society and Make the Road New York said, according to amNY.

The attorneys said he is being held in harsh conditions, reportedly in solitary confinement, at the Metropolitan Detention Center in Sunset Park, Brooklyn, and has had only water from a bathroom sink, amNY reported. He was taken from NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital in an ICE vehicle after the shooting while police pushed back protesters.

According to his lawyers, he has numbness on the left side of his face, hearing problems in his left ear and a shoulder wound from broken glass. Doctors said he urgently needs surgery but considered it too dangerous without a specialized surgeon, and it is unclear whether it will take place, amNY reported.

The attorneys accused ICE of deliberate indifference and due process violations and filed a habeas corpus petition that prevents his immediate deportation or removal from New York. The Department of Homeland Security maintains that he is a criminal and a member of the Trinitarios gang, according to amNY.
Mayor Zohran Mamdani, speaking on MS NOW on Sunday, compared the chaos on the street to a mass shooting. As of the report, the man remained in detention awaiting legal proceedings.

sources.title: ICE SHOOTING: Marble Hill detainee still has bullet in his neck, has not eaten while in custody, attorneys say

stories.title: Gowanus Open Studios Turns 30 as Rising Rents Squeeze Artists Out
stories.dek: The free studio weekend marks its 30th edition as development since the 2021 rezoning pressures working artists in Gowanus.
body: Gowanus Open Studios, the free weekend when neighborhood artists open their workspaces to the public, was scheduled for its 30th edition on Oct. 17 and 18 from noon to 6 p.m., Hoodline reported. The nonprofit Arts Gowanus organizes the event, which reports have put at 400 to 500 artists across about 90 to 100 locations.

The tour began in 1996 as the Gowanus Annual Studio Tour, with 543 Union Street considered its birthplace. Artist JoAnne McFarland, who has kept a studio there since the 1990s, told ARTHAG NYC she worries neighborhood changes could eventually force her out, according to Hoodline.

For the first time, visitors can see 15 subsidized studios at 420 Carroll Street and 498 Sackett Street, created through an agreement between Arts Gowanus and developers. Rents start at $20 per square foot a year and can rise no more than 2% annually after the second year, according to Arts Gowanus.

Development has accelerated since the 2021 rezoning. Curbed reported that dozens of rental buildings have gone up and the area is expected to add 9,000 housing units by the end of the decade, Hoodline said. A CreateNYC survey found 76% of artist respondents named cost or space as their main challenge.

Arts Gowanus executive director Johnny Thornton said he hopes the event continues for another 30 years. This year's program includes a 30-artist anniversary show at Union Channel and a screening of the documentary Gowanus Current at 420 Carroll Street.

sources.title: Gowanus Open Studios Marks 30 Years as Rising Rents Squeeze Artists Out

stories.title: Mamdani Says ICE Agent Looked Like a Mass Shooter at Marble Hill Stop
stories.dek: The mayor criticized the federal agent who opened fire during an Oct. 8 traffic stop in Marble Hill as footage of the encounter emerged.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Sunday that the ICE agent who shot a 28-year-old driver during a traffic stop in Marble Hill looked like a mass shooter, amNY reported. The man's 5-year-old child was in the car during the Oct. 8 shooting.

NYPD body camera footage shows officers arriving to find an ICE agent in a construction vest holding a long gun, according to amNY. Surveillance video shows an agent rushing toward the man's Honda with a gun displayed, but does not clearly show whether he identified himself as a federal officer. The driver pulled away as shots were fired and pedestrians ducked for cover.

Speaking on MS NOW's Connect with Jacob Soboroff, Mamdani said ICE treats the law as optional and that bystanders were unsure what they were seeing, amNY reported. He has said he tried to negotiate the man's release with President Trump without reaching an agreement.

amNY reported that the same agent was seen during an October 2025 federal raid on Canal Street, detaining immigrants at court hearings and in Minneapolis. The Department of Homeland Security says the wounded man is associated with the Trinitarios gang. The FBI is investigating the shooting, according to amNY.

Protests followed, and Darializa Avila Chevalier, the Democratic nominee for Congress, was pushed to the ground during clashes with police. She called on Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch to resign. Sources told amNY that Tisch has no plans to step down and Mamdani does not intend to ask her to.

sources.title: Mamdani: ICE agent looked like 'mass shooter' in Marble Hill traffic stop

stories.title: Mamdani Says Talks With Trump Failed to Free Man Shot by ICE Agents
stories.dek: Federal agents removed the wounded man from a Manhattan hospital after the mayor's appeals to President Trump and DHS were unsuccessful.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Thursday night that talks with President Trump and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin failed to win the release of a 28-year-old man shot by federal immigration agents in Marble Hill, amNY reported. Mamdani said agents then removed the man from NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital in an unmarked vehicle.

The shooting happened shortly after 4 p.m. on Oct. 8 near 2 Marble Hill Ave., where agents were trying to take the man into custody, according to amNY. Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said at least one ICE agent fired seven rounds, striking the driver in the neck. A 5-year-old boy in the vehicle was unharmed and is with a family member.

Surveillance video showed a plainclothes officer approaching the driver's window with a drawn gun before the vehicle moved out of view, amNY reported; the cameras did not capture the shooting. NYPD officers responding to an unrelated call found the man handcuffed on the ground and took him to the hospital in stable condition. Tisch said the NYPD had no involvement in the federal operation.

The Department of Homeland Security said officers were conducting a targeted arrest of a Dominican national with a prior grand larceny conviction and claimed gang ties, which amNY said it had not verified. DHS did not say what prompted the shots or whether the man was armed.

Mamdani called the shooting an outrage and renewed his call to abolish ICE. Gov. Kathy Hochul said she urged Trump and Mullin to halt enforcement in New York and release body camera footage. Federal agents have taken control of the investigation.

sources.title: ICE SHOOTING: Mamdani says talks with Trump failed to free man wounded by agents who fired seven shots in Marble Hill

stories.title: Manhattan Prosecutors Push to Keep State Case Against Mangione Alive
stories.dek: Prosecutors argued that Luigi Mangione's federal guilty plea should not end the state murder case over the 2024 killing of a health insurance executive.
body: Manhattan prosecutors asked a court Friday to let their state murder case against Luigi Mangione proceed despite his guilty plea in federal court, according to an Associated Press report published by NY1.

The state case concerns the December 2024 killing of UnitedHealthcare CEO Brian Thompson on a Manhattan street. In a court filing, Assistant District Attorney Joel Seidemann and colleagues argued that the state and federal cases involve different harms, purposes and crimes, so double jeopardy does not apply, the AP reported.
Mangione's lawyers are seeking dismissal of the state murder and weapons charges, arguing he is being prosecuted twice for the same event. A ruling is expected in late autumn, according to the AP.

In August, Mangione pleaded guilty to federal stalking and cyberstalking charges and admitted traveling to New York to carry out the killing, the AP reported. He pleaded not guilty in 2024 to the state murder, weapons and fake-ID charges, and his federal admission could be used against him if the state case goes to trial.
The ruling will determine whether Mangione, 28, faces a state trial in Manhattan and how much prison time a state conviction could add to a likely lengthy federal sentence, according to the AP.

sources.title: New York prosecutors seek to sustain their case against Luigi Mangione, despite his federal plea

stories.title: Homeland Security Secretary Offers Murky Account of Marble Hill Shooting
stories.dek: Secretary Markwayne Mullin described calls with the mayor and governor after the ICE shooting and made a claim about Mamdani that amNY reported was false.
body: Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin gave an unclear account Friday of his and President Trump's calls with Gov. Kathy Hochul and Mayor Zohran Mamdani about the Oct. 8 ICE shooting in Marble Hill, amNY reported.

At a press conference, Mullin said Trump offered to transfer the wounded man to NYPD custody if the city pursued charges, and that Mamdani replied the city would not detain him, according to amNY. Mullin did not specify which charges he meant.

Mullin also said Hochul offered help with more than 100 criminals. A person familiar with the call told amNY that she was referring to more than 100 crimes for which the NYPD could cooperate with federal authorities, not 100 people.

Mullin said the mayor had said nothing about the Oct. 2 stabbing of an off-duty NYPD detective in the Bronx. amNY reported that claim was false, noting Mamdani visited the detective at Jacobi Hospital with Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch that day and posted a statement about the attack.

Mullin said Mamdani's words incite hostility. amNY reported that the mayor's remarks did not call for violence. City Hall had not responded to a request for comment on Mullin's account as of publication.

sources.title: ICE SHOOTING: Homeland Security Secretary Mullin offers murky account of events, false claims about Mamdani response to stabbed cop

stories.title: Judges Hear 9/11 Families' Case Against Saudi Arabia
stories.dek: A federal appeals panel in Manhattan heard arguments on whether U.S. courts have jurisdiction over families' claims that Saudi Arabia aided the Sept. 11 hijackers.
body: A three-judge panel of the U.S. Court of Appeals in Manhattan heard arguments Wednesday in the long-running lawsuit by families of people killed on Sept. 11, 2001, who argue the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia helped the attackers, NY1 reported.

The panel is considering only whether federal courts have jurisdiction over Saudi Arabia, which holds sovereign immunity as a nation, according to NY1. A law Congress passed 10 years ago made the suit possible. A year earlier, a federal judge denied the kingdom's motion to dismiss.

The families, including members of 9/11 Justice and 9/11 Families United, claim that men who worked for Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Islamic Affairs helped at least two hijackers, including by finding them housing in San Diego, and knew of the plot, NY1 reported. The families are seeking billions of dollars.

A lawyer for the Saudi government told the panel that the kingdom has never supported al-Qaida and is a U.S. ally. Brett Eagleson, president of 9/11 Justice, who lost his father in the attacks, called the kingdom's position a desperate attempt to avoid accountability, according to NY1. Terry Strada, national chair of 9/11 Families United, urged President Trump to side with the families.

The Saudi consulate did not respond to NY1's request for comment, and lawyers for both sides declined interviews. The appeals court did not say when it will rule. The families hope a trial will begin within the next year.

sources.title: Judges hear arguments in case of Sept. 11 families suing Kingdom of Saudi Arabia

stories.title: Pro-Palestinian Protesters Disrupt Oct. 7 Vigil, Heckle Mamdani
stories.dek: About 200 demonstrators interrupted a Union Square vigil marking the 2023 Hamas attack and jeered Mayor Zohran Mamdani.
body: About 200 pro-Palestinian demonstrators disrupted a Union Square vigil Wednesday night marking the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas attack on Israel and jeered Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who attended, amNY reported.

The vigil was organized by Israelis for Peace, whose roughly 50 members were outnumbered, according to amNY. Organizers said it also remembered Palestinians killed in the Gaza war. The protesters gathered at City Hall Park shortly after 4 p.m. and reached Union Square around 6:30 p.m.

When speakers tried to read statements from people who had experienced trauma in the Middle East, protesters chanted in support of Hamas, and the speeches were postponed, amNY reported. Police set up metal barricades to separate the groups. Public Advocate Jumaane Williams appealed for a space that honored everyone's pain; former Comptroller Brad Lander also attended.

Protesters called Mamdani a traitor and a sellout, according to amNY. Earlier that day he had issued a statement sympathizing with Oct. 7 victims that also condemned what he called genocide by the Israeli government in Gaza. He stayed until the end and spoke, and protesters followed his motorcade as he left.
Gov. Kathy Hochul posted that disrupting the vigil while waving terrorist flags was absolutely despicable. As of publication, Mamdani had not commented publicly on the incident, amNY reported.

sources.title: Mayor Mamdani jeered as 'traitor' by pro-Palestine protesters who crashed Oct. 7 vigil, chanted support for terrorists as New Yorkers mourn

stories.title: Shuttered Cobble Hill Firehouse to Become $17.8M Music Center
stories.dek: Work has begun on converting the former Engine 204 firehouse, closed since 2003, into a permanent home for the Noel Pointer Foundation's free music programs.
body: City officials broke ground Tuesday on the conversion of the former Engine Company 204 firehouse at 299 Degraw Street in Cobble Hill into a permanent home for the Noel Pointer Foundation, a nonprofit offering free music education, Hoodline reported. The project budget is $17.8 million.

The firehouse was closed in 2003 during budget cuts under Mayor Michael Bloomberg and sat vacant for years, according to Hoodline, citing PIX11 and DNAinfo. A 2007 plan to move the Brooklyn Philharmonic's offices there collapsed when the orchestra faced insolvency.

City funding began in 2019 with an initial $6.5 million, and the mayor's office, City Council and Brooklyn Borough President's office now back the project, Hoodline reported. In July, the Department of Design and Construction awarded a $10.3 million contract to APN Construction Corp. of Woodside. Plans for the 6,000-square-foot building include soundproofed classrooms, recording studios, a performance hall and a garden.

The foundation, started in 1995 by Chinita Pointer in honor of her late husband, jazz violinist Noel Pointer, serves about 2,000 students a year, according to Hoodline. The new space will add piano, guitar, voice, DJing and composition to its string programs.
Construction is expected to take about two years, according to PIX11, as cited by Hoodline.

sources.title: Cobble Hill Firehouse Shuttered Since 2003 Reborn as $17.8M Music School

stories.title: Firefighter Who Died at Brooklyn Fire Honored at FDNY Memorial
stories.dek: Lt. Patrick Brady of Ladder 120 was among 11 FDNY members whose names were added to the department's Upper Manhattan memorial.
body: FDNY Lt. Patrick Brady, who died after a medical emergency while working a Brooklyn fire last year, was honored Wednesday as his name was added to the department's memorial on Riverside Drive, amNY reported.

The annual ceremony at the Firemen's Memorial at West 100th Street and Riverside Drive added the names of 11 active or retired members who died over the past year, according to amNY. Thousands of firefighters attended, along with Fire Commissioner Lillian Bonsignore and Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

Brady, of Ladder Company 120, suffered a medical episode on a roof at 9407 Kings Highway on Nov. 8, 2025, went into cardiac arrest and could not be revived, amNY reported. He joined the FDNY in 2014, served at Engine 227 and transferred to Ladder 120 in 2022.

Mamdani presented Brady's widow with the FDNY flag, and the commissioner presented the department's medal of valor, according to amNY. Ladder 120 commander Chris Hagen described Brady as a skilled firefighter and a good teacher to younger members. Mamdani noted that nearly 1,200 FDNY members have died in service to the city.
Paramedic Salih Abdur Rahman, who died on Oct. 29, 2025, after finishing a shift at the FDNY Training Academy on Randall's Island, was also honored.

sources.title: Firefighter who died battling Brooklyn blaze receives posthumous honors at FDNY's Upper Manhattan Memorial

stories.title: Court Orders Teksupport and Parent Firm to Cease Operations After Nov. 7
stories.dek: A New Jersey court order requires TCE Presents, parent of the New York party promoter Teksupport, to stop holding events and liquidate its assets.
body: A New Jersey court has ordered TCE Presents, the parent company of New York promoter Teksupport, to stop holding events under any of its brands starting Nov. 7, Resident Advisor reported.
The order, filed Oct. 5, requires non-essential TCE employees to be terminated by Oct. 9, the company's assets to be liquidated and related entities to be frozen, according to RA.

The ruling follows a dispute between TCE cofounders Robert Toma and Michael Vitacco, who started the company in 2010, RA reported. Each filed a lawsuit in New Jersey earlier this year accusing the other of undermining his role, and both are seeking sole ownership and damages. In March, a court granted a temporary restraining order in Vitacco's favor barring Toma from interfering with operations, and the two have since been in mediation.

Teksupport is known for warehouse parties and for bringing European nightlife brands including Time Warp, CircoLoco and DGTL to New York. It has events scheduled at Brooklyn Storehouse on Oct. 30 and 31 and at The Chocolate Factory on Nov. 6, and RA said it was unclear whether they will proceed. Brooklyn Storehouse, a joint operation of TCE Presents and Broadwick Live, has said it will close after Oct. 31.
RA said it contacted TCE Presents for comment and had not received a reply at publication.

sources.title: New York promoter Teksupport and parent firm ordered to cease operations

stories.title: NYC Crime Hits Historic Lows Through Nine Months, but Hate Crimes Rise
stories.dek: NYPD figures show major crime and murders falling through September while reported hate crimes climbed nearly 13 percent.
body: Major crime in New York City fell 9.4% in the third quarter compared with a year earlier, driven by a 19.8% drop in murders, from 91 to 73, according to NYPD data reported by NY1. Reported hate crimes, however, rose.

From July 1 to Sept. 30, car thefts fell 17.1%, robberies 13.6%, burglaries 11.7% and grand larcenies 10.2%, NY1 reported. Shooting incidents dropped 22.7%. Year to date, major crime is down 6.6%, and murders fell from 253 to 203.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said at a briefing that the first nine months and the third quarter had the fewest shootings, shooting victims and murders on record for the five boroughs. She credited the department's precision policing strategy, including removing illegal guns and dismantling gangs, according to NY1.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani said September set record lows for shootings but cautioned that work remains, naming hate crimes as a key concern. Hate crimes rose 12.6% in the quarter and 12.9% year to date, NY1 reported.

Anti-Jewish incidents made up 52.9% of confirmed hate crimes through September, with 245 reported compared with 242 a year earlier, though they fell 13.2% in the third quarter alone. Anti-Muslim hate crimes rose from 18 to 32 year to date, according to NY1.

sources.title: NYC continues to see historic crime lows, but hate crimes rise

stories.title: Staten Island Lands First Community Justice Center With $20 Million
stories.dek: State and city funding will convert a former Stapleton courthouse into the borough's first permanent community justice center.
body: New York State has committed $15 million to convert a former courthouse at 67 Targee Street in Stapleton into Staten Island's first permanent community justice center, Hoodline reported, citing an announcement by Gov. Kathy Hochul.

The state money adds to a $5 million city capital grant secured by Council Member Kamillah Hanks in 2024, for a combined $20 million, according to Hoodline. The building was constructed in the 1920s as the Richmond County Criminal Courthouse.

Staten Island is the only borough without a permanent community justice center, Hoodline reported. District Attorney Michael McMahon said the borough had been the only one without such a center underway and praised the investment. The Center for Justice Innovation has run diversion and alternatives-to-incarceration programs from an interim office at 30 Beach Street.

The new center is planned to offer screening, case management and referrals for mental health, substance use, housing and employment, along with youth diversion, violence prevention and victim services, according to Hoodline. The governor's office credited State Sen. Jessica Scarcella-Spanton and Assembly Member Charles Fall with advocating for the funding.
No construction start date, completion timeline or operating budget had been specified as of the announcement, Hoodline reported, citing the Utica Phoenix.

sources.title: Staten Island Lands First Community Justice Center With $20 Million in Combined Funding

stories.title: Ticketing Company Posh to Open Its First New York Venue
stories.dek: A job posting shows the nightlife ticketing firm plans a brick-and-mortar space as a prototype for a national concept.
body: Posh, a New York-based ticketing company focused on nightlife events, is planning to open a venue in the city, its first brick-and-mortar space, Resident Advisor reported, citing a public LinkedIn job post published Oct. 2.

According to the job post, the venue will host public and private events and will be offered as an exclusive perk to Posh's top promoters, RA reported. The company aims for the venue to break even monthly in its first year, and the space is described as a prototype for a nationwide concept.
The venue's name and location have not been announced, and it is unconfirmed whether it will use Posh's own ticketing service, according to RA.

Posh is seven years old, operates in major U.S. cities and is backed by several venture capital investors, RA reported. It describes itself as a social networking platform and shows users events attended by friends and mutual connections.
RA said it had contacted Posh for more information. The report included no statement from the company.

sources.title: US ticketing company Posh to open New York venue

stories.title: City Rent Freeze Takes Effect as Legal Fight Continues
stories.dek: Tenants renewing rent-stabilized leases will pay the same rent as last year while a lawsuit challenges the Rent Guidelines Board's vote.
body: A freeze on rents for the city's roughly 1 million rent-stabilized apartments has taken effect, NY1 reported, meaning tenants renewing a stabilized lease will receive an offer at the same rent they paid the previous year.
The Rent Guidelines Board voted in June to approve a 0% increase for both one-year and two-year leases, according to NY1. The freeze was a key campaign promise of Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

The measure faces an ongoing lawsuit that seeks to overturn the board's decision and argues that Mamdani improperly influenced it, NY1 reported. In September, Staten Island Judge Brendan T. Lantry ordered the city to turn over written communications between mayor's office and board staff from Jan. 1 to June 25, 2026, writing that the allegations raised significant concern about the lawfulness of the board's procedure.

Landlords hope a final ruling will force the board to reconsider and approve an increase, according to NY1. Landlord advocate Kenny Burgos warned that limiting building revenue while costs rise could lower housing quality for many tenants. Some tenants told NY1 that the freeze makes it easier to budget and plan.
The Mamdani administration maintains that the board acted appropriately and reviewed all the data presented to it. The court has not issued a final decision.

sources.title: NYC rent freeze takes effect amid ongoing legal challenge

stories.title: City Unveils Plan to Combat Antisemitism
stories.dek: Mayor Zohran Mamdani released a long-awaited plan to prevent hate crimes against Jewish New Yorkers as hate crimes rise across the city.
body: Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a long-awaited plan on Tuesday to combat antisemitism in New York City, NY1 reported. The announcement came as hate crimes rise across the five boroughs and Jewish New Yorkers have growing concerns, according to the outlet.

The plan lays out several ways the city will invest in preventing hate crimes against the Jewish community, NY1 reported. One of its named components is a public messaging effort that highlights the contributions of Jewish New Yorkers to the city.

Phylisa Wisdom, executive director of the Mayor's Office to Combat Antisemitism, discussed the plan on Wednesday in an interview on NY1's Inside City Hall with political anchor Errol Louis, according to the outlet.

NY1's report did not include dollar amounts, a timeline for putting the measures in place, or program details beyond the messaging effort. It also did not include direct quotes from city officials about the plan.
The plan has been announced, but its implementation has not yet been reported.

sources.title: NYC announces plan to combat antisemitism

stories.title: Federal Judge Strikes Down ICE Courthouse Arrest Policy Nationwide
stories.dek: Judge P. Kevin Castel ruled that the policy behind mass arrests at immigration courts, including at 26 Federal Plaza, was arbitrary and capricious.
body: U.S. District Judge P. Kevin Castel on Oct. 1 struck down an ICE policy that led to mass detentions inside immigration courthouses, including hundreds at 26 Federal Plaza in Lower Manhattan, amNY reported. The ruling applies nationwide and took effect immediately.

Castel found the legal basis for the detentions arbitrary and capricious, according to amNY. ICE must now return to a 2021 policy that allows arrests at or near immigration courts only in limited circumstances.

The lawsuit was filed Aug. 1, 2025, by a coalition including the New York Civil Liberties Union, the ACLU and Make the Road New York, amNY reported. In a March filing, then-U.S. Attorney Jay Clayton and the NYCLU said ICE had misrepresented its authority to make arrests inside immigration courts. The final ruling affirms an earlier stay and extends it nationwide.

Amy Belsher of the NYCLU called the decision a major win for noncitizens attending their hearings, and Harold Solis of Make the Road New York said it ends the practice of arresting immigrants for showing up to court, according to amNY.

Courthouse sources told amNY that arrests have slowed but still occur, with one reported the week before the ruling, and that fear of detention led some people to skip hearings. Under federal law, those who miss hearings can be ordered removed in absentia. amNY did not report an appeal.

sources.title: Federal judge strikes down ICE immigration courthouse arrest policy across the country

stories.title: LCD Soundsystem Announces 12-Show Holiday Residency at Knockdown Center and Brooklyn Steel
stories.dek: The band's annual New York residency will include its 100th residency show, with proceeds from that night going to charity.
body: LCD Soundsystem has announced its annual holiday residency in New York, a 12-show run split between Knockdown Center in Maspeth and Brooklyn Steel in East Williamsburg, Resident Advisor reported.
The band will play eight shows at Knockdown Center, on Nov. 19 to 22 and Dec. 10 to 13, and four at Brooklyn Steel, from Nov. 30 to Dec. 3, according to RA. Openers and DJs have not been announced.

The Nov. 30 show at Brooklyn Steel will be the band's 100th residency show, RA reported. The residency tradition began in 2021. For that night, the band will donate all ticket proceeds to a charity that has not yet been named.

The band has not released new material since the 2024 single "x-ray eyes," according to RA, but toured the U.S. and Europe this year. It is scheduled to open for Harry Styles at a show in Rome and has three New Year's Eve dates in Aspen, Colorado.
Separately, guitarist Al Doyle, who also plays in Hot Chip, announced his debut solo album, Hollywood Saviour, due Nov. 20 on DFA Records, RA reported.

sources.title: LCD Soundsystem announces annual holiday New York residency

stories.title: Federal Monitor Finds Nearly 10,000 NYPD Street Stops Missing From Records
stories.dek: The court-appointed stop-and-frisk monitor estimated that about one in four NYPD investigative stops in 2025 went undocumented.
body: The court-appointed monitor overseeing NYPD stop-and-frisk reforms reported that officers failed to properly document nearly 10,000 investigative stops in 2025, amNY reported.

According to the report by monitor Mylan L. Denerstein, 9,641 so-called Terry stops were not documented and 25,936 were, meaning roughly one in four went unrecorded, amNY reported. A Terry stop, based on reasonable suspicion, allows officers to briefly detain someone and requires a formal stop report.

The monitor's team reviewed body camera footage and found officers had recorded some of these stops as lower-level encounters that do not require paperwork, according to amNY. Underreporting fell to 18.4% in the fourth quarter of 2025, against an estimated 27.1% for the full year.

The NYPD acknowledged more work is needed but said the trend is improving, noting reported stops fell from more than 680,000 in 2011 to fewer than 30,000 in 2025, amNY reported. Legal Aid Society attorney Karina Tefft called the findings a fundamental accountability failure, and attorney Jonathan Moore urged the court to take aggressive action.
The report has been released. amNY did not report any court ruling or remedy in response.

sources.title: Nearly 10,000 NYPD street stops went missing from department books, federal monitor says

stories.title: Brooklyn Commuter Killed After Bag Caught in A Train Doors
stories.dek: A 57-year-old man died at the Utica Avenue station after a departing A train dragged him along the platform, police sources said.
body: A 57-year-old man was killed Monday evening at the Utica Avenue A train station in Brooklyn after a bag he was carrying got caught in the doors of a departing train, amNY reported, citing police sources.

The incident happened at about 5:48 p.m. on Sept. 28 on the Manhattan-bound platform, according to amNY. Police sources said the train began moving and dragged the man along the platform. He had difficulty walking, used a cane and tried to alert the conductor by hitting the doors, sources said.
The motorman did not realize what had happened until it was too late, according to a preliminary investigation cited by amNY. Police described the death as an apparent accident.
NYPD Transit District 33 and EMS responded, and the man was pronounced dead shortly after 6 p.m., amNY reported. Police sources said no criminality is suspected.
The investigation is ongoing. amNY said it had asked the MTA for comment and was awaiting a response at publication.

sources.title: Brooklyn commuter dragged to his death by A train after his bag gets caught in doors banged on door with cane moments before demise

stories.title: Woman Killed in Hit-and-Run While Biking on 34th Street
stories.dek: A cyclist was struck and killed by a dump truck in Midtown, and the driver was later taken into custody, police said.
body: A woman riding an e-bike was struck and killed by a dump truck on West 34th Street in Midtown on Monday morning, and the driver kept going, amNY reported, citing police.

The crash happened just before 11 a.m. on Sept. 28 between Seventh and Eighth avenues as the woman rode westbound on a wet street, according to amNY. Police first described her as a teenager, then said she was 51. Transportation Alternatives said she was a delivery worker. EMS pronounced her dead at the scene.

The dump truck was later found at Fifth Avenue and 35th Street, where the driver was detained, given a sobriety test and taken into custody, amNY reported. No charges had been filed at publication, and the result of the sobriety test was not reported. Officers from the Midtown South Precinct and the NYPD Collision Investigation Squad responded.

Transportation Alternatives executive director Ben Furnas said she was the 20th bike rider killed in the city this year, including 17 e-bike riders, and that the death was the 149th traffic fatality citywide this year, according to amNY. He criticized the lack of bike infrastructure on 34th Street and noted a City Council hearing on e-bikes scheduled within days.
amNY described the case as a developing story. The driver's identity and any charges had not been reported.

sources.title: Horror on 34th Street: Woman killed in hit-and-run while riding bike in Midtown, cops say

stories.title: NYPD Releases Bodycam Video of Fatal Times Square Police Shooting
stories.dek: Footage released by the NYPD appears to show a woman accused of stabbing two people saying she wanted to die before officers shot her.
body: The NYPD on Sept. 25 released body camera footage of the Aug. 31 fatal police shooting of a woman in Times Square, and the video appears to show her expressing an intention to be killed by officers, amNY reported.

Police said the 49-year-old Queens woman stabbed two people near a subway entrance at West 43rd Street and Seventh Avenue in what witnesses described as unprovoked attacks, according to amNY. A 32-year-old woman died at Bellevue Hospital, and a 68-year-old man survived, law enforcement sources said.

Two officers encountered the woman at about 4:25 p.m. on Seventh Avenue near the NYPD substation while she still held two knives, amNY reported. One officer tried to talk her down with guns holstered, and the footage captures her saying this was the only way out.

At about 4:29 p.m., additional officers arrived and two fired Tasers, which were ineffective, according to amNY. When the woman advanced toward officers with the knives, two officers fired about three shots. She was pronounced dead at Bellevue Hospital.

Police Commissioner Jessica Tisch said the officers did what they were trained to do. The footage came out less than a month after the shooting, amid Mayor Zohran Mamdani's pledge to release police video faster. amNY reported no findings or final determinations on the shooting.

sources.title: NYPD bodycam video of deadly Times Square shooting indicates woman expressed 'suicide-by-cop' intentions after stabbing rampage

stories.title: Over 100 Arrested at Netanyahu Protest; Councilman Chi Ossé Detained
stories.dek: Police arrested more than 100 people at Midtown protests against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's U.N. address, including a sitting council member.
body: Police arrested more than 100 people Thursday at protests in Midtown Manhattan against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was scheduled to address the U.N. General Assembly at 2 p.m., Hoodline reported.

City Council Member Chi Ossé was taken into custody at First Avenue and East 39th Street, according to Hoodline, citing the New York Daily News. Demonstrators had planned a march from Bryant Park to U.N. headquarters on East 46th Street.

Mayor Zohran Mamdani criticized Netanyahu and called him a war criminal but said he would not join the protests, while encouraging peaceful demonstration, Hoodline reported. The International Criminal Court has accused Netanyahu of war crimes related to Gaza, according to the Daily News.

Protests have accompanied Netanyahu's recent visits to New York. More than 50 people were arrested at a Midtown protest in September 2024, according to NBC New York, as cited by Hoodline. The city had designated Sept. 21 to 25 as Gridlock Alert Days for U.N. General Assembly week.
Hoodline did not report charges, releases or any other outcome for those arrested, including Ossé.

sources.title: Over 100 Arrested at Netanyahu Protest, Councilman Chi Ossé Cuffed

stories.title: Two-Alarm Bronx Fire Leaves One Dead, Another Hurt After Window Jump
stories.dek: A fire in a six-story Montgomery Avenue apartment building killed one person and injured more than a dozen others, including four firefighters.
body: A two-alarm fire in a six-story apartment building at 1484 Montgomery Avenue in the Bronx left one person dead and others injured Wednesday morning, amNY reported. The fire broke out at about 7:45 a.m. on Sept. 23.

A 31-year-old man jumped from a window to escape the fire and was taken to Jacobi Hospital in critical but stable condition, according to the FDNY. Fire officials said at least 10 other people were hurt, along with four firefighters. After the fire was under control, responders found an unidentified adult who was pronounced dead at the scene, amNY reported.
FDNY Deputy Chief Andrew Holzmaier said the fire spread quickly to nearby apartments and the roof, mostly through bathroom walls where pipes and electrical wiring run, according to amNY.
The FDNY said a vehicle blocking a hydrant in front of the building slowed the response. The Bureau of Fire Prevention issued summonses totaling $4,000 and towed the vehicle, amNY reported.

Sources told amNY that a man was seen in a hallway with an incendiary device before the fire, but fire marshals have not determined the cause. No arrests had been reported, and the investigation is ongoing.

sources.title: Two-alarm Bronx fire leaves one dead, another injured after jumping from window

stories.title: Loew's Paradise Theatre Set to Return as 4,000-Seat Arts Hub
stories.dek: The landmark Grand Concourse movie palace, vacant since 2023, is being revived as the nonprofit Paradise Performing Arts Center.
body: The Loew's Paradise Theatre on the Grand Concourse in the Bronx, closed to the public since 2023, is being turned into the nonprofit Paradise Performing Arts Center, Hoodline reported. Organizers plan concerts, comedy, dance, film and educational programs.

A community welcome event with self-guided tours is set for Nov. 10, according to Hoodline, citing Bronx Times, and the center's website says the venue will reopen in November 2026. With about 4,000 seats, the center describes it as the second-largest theater in the city after Radio City Music Hall.

The theater opened on Sept. 7, 1929, as one of five Loew's Wonder Theatres in the New York area, Hoodline reported. It closed in 1994, later served as an event space and a church, and reopened as a live venue in 2005 before falling vacant again. Its exterior was landmarked in 1997 and its interior in 2006.

Executive director Scott Perrin said every borough except the Bronx has a major performing arts center and that the venue would expand access in an underserved neighborhood, according to Hoodline. Peter Martin and Charles Piazza are managing directors.
The center says it is in talks with philanthropic supporters, corporate sponsors and elected officials to build a sustainable programming model. The venue had not yet reopened as of the report.

sources.title: Bronx's Grand Loew's Paradise Theatre Roars Back as 4,000-Seat Arts Hub

stories.title: Woman, 68, Slashed in Sheepshead Bay Subway Door Dispute
stories.dek: A man who had propped open an emergency exit door allegedly cut a 68-year-old woman's face with a knife, and a person of interest was taken into custody.
body: A 68-year-old woman was slashed in the face Saturday morning at the Sheepshead Bay B/Q subway station after a dispute with a man who had propped open an emergency exit door, Hoodline reported.
The dispute began at about 9 a.m., according to Hoodline. The man allegedly held a knife to the woman's face, cutting her, then ran onto the platform and boarded a southbound Q train.

NYPD Transit officers took a 70-year-old man into custody at the station, Hoodline reported. He was described as a person of interest, and charges were pending as of the report. The woman refused medical attention at the scene.

People sometimes prop open the exit-only doors to ask riders for money, according to the New York Post, as cited by Hoodline. NYPD data cited by the Post showed felony assault complaints in the transit system rose 12% this year as of Oct. 13, from 470 to 525.
Hoodline reported that a stabbing outside a lounge on Avenue U a week earlier was unrelated. The man in custody has not been charged and is presumed innocent.

sources.title: Sheepshead Bay Subway Door Dispute Ends With 68-Year-Old Woman Slashed

stories.title: Man Shot in Leg Near Bed-Stuy School; Students Shelter in Place
stories.dek: A man sitting in a car at Monroe Street and Ralph Avenue was shot in the leg, and a nearby school kept students inside as a precaution.
body: A man was shot in the leg while sitting in a car at Monroe Street and Ralph Avenue in Bedford-Stuyvesant just after 1 p.m. Tuesday, Hoodline reported, citing police via News12.
The man was taken to Wyckoff Hospital, according to Hoodline. His age and condition were not reported.

A school near P.S. 309, a few blocks from the shooting, went into shelter-in-place while police responded, keeping students and staff inside as a precaution, Hoodline reported. No students were hurt, and school staff said the order was lifted later the same day.

Police had not announced any arrests or released a description of a suspect as of the latest reporting, according to Hoodline. The outlet attributed details of the shooting to police, through News12, and the status of the school to school staff.
The shooting remains under investigation. Hoodline noted that a January shooting on Marcus Garvey Boulevard also prompted a lockdown at a nearby Success Academy school, according to News12.

sources.title: Bed-Stuy School Shelters in Place After Man Shot in Leg Nearby

stories.title: Four Men Beat Driver With Pipe and Steal His SUV in East Williamsburg
stories.dek: Police released images of four men sought in an Oct. 6 carjacking outside 364 Ten Eyck Street.
body: Police are searching for four men who beat a 27-year-old driver with a metal pipe and stole his SUV in East Williamsburg, Hoodline reported.

The attack happened at about 1 a.m. on Oct. 6 outside 364 Ten Eyck Street, according to Hoodline. Citing News12 New York, the outlet reported that the four men surrounded the man's blue 2026 Toyota Highlander, forced him out, punched him in the face and struck him with the pipe.
The men took his car keys, cellphone and a wallet containing $200, then drove off south on Morgan Street in the Highlander, Hoodline reported. The driver was treated at the scene.
Police released images of the four men, who were wearing dark hooded sweatshirts or jackets, according to Hoodline. The area is covered by the NYPD's 90th Precinct.
No arrests had been reported as of Hoodline's report. Investigators asked anyone with information to come forward or contact NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Four Men Beat Driver With Pipe, Steal His SUV In East Williamsburg

stories.title: Teenager Slashed in Ridgewood Morning Assault; Suspect at Large
stories.dek: A 17-year-old was cut on the hand near Myrtle and Forest avenues, and police are searching for a young suspect who fled on foot.
body: Police in Queens are searching for a suspect who slashed a 17-year-old boy near Myrtle and Forest avenues in Ridgewood on Monday morning, amNY reported.

The attack happened at about 7:50 a.m. on Oct. 19, according to amNY. Officers from the 104th Precinct found the teen with a cut to his right hand, and EMS took him to Bellevue Hospital, where he was listed in stable condition.
Police do not yet know what led to the attack, amNY reported. Based on a preliminary investigation, police sources said the suspect may have known the victim.

Police described the suspect as a male aged 17 to 18, last seen wearing a black hooded sweatshirt with a spider logo and carrying a Nike backpack. He fled south on Forest Avenue and remains at large, according to amNY.
The 104th Precinct has recorded 263 assaults this year through Oct. 11, up 14.3% from the same point in 2025, amNY reported. Anyone with information can call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Queens teenager slashed in morning assault; young suspect still on run, cops say

stories.title: Fresh Meadows Man Indicted on Hate Crime Charges Over Bagel Shop Vandalism
stories.dek: Prosecutors say a 22-year-old twice damaged planters outside a kosher bagel shop on Union Turnpike that displayed Israeli flags.
body: A 22-year-old Fresh Meadows man was indicted on two counts of third-degree criminal mischief as a hate crime, accused of vandalizing a kosher bagel shop on Union Turnpike that displayed Israeli flags, QNS reported, citing the Queens District Attorney's Office.

Dawood Faisal was arraigned Oct. 19 in Queens Supreme Court, according to QNS. Prosecutors allege that at about 6:18 p.m. on May 15 he knocked over nine metal plant stands outside Bagels & Co. at 188-02 Union Turnpike and threw the debris at the shop.
Prosecutors further allege that at about 1 a.m. on May 23 he pushed and kicked over 11 plant stands, then pulled plants from a large clay pot by hand, QNS reported.

Queens District Attorney Melinda Katz said he allegedly targeted the business because it is Jewish-owned and displayed Israeli flags, calling bias crimes an affront to the community. The charge is not bail-eligible, and Justice Michael Hartofilis ordered him to return to court Nov. 12. He faces up to seven years in prison if convicted, according to QNS.

Faisal is separately charged with manslaughter and assault in a May 25 crash near Cunningham Park that killed a 71-year-old woman, and is being held without bail in that case, QNS reported. He is presumed innocent in both cases.

sources.title: Fresh Meadows man indicted on hate crime charge for allegedly vandalizing Jewish-owned bagel shop displaying Israeli flags: DA

stories.title: Upper East Side Bank Vandalized; NYPD Probes Possible Hate Crime
stories.dek: Windows at a Capital One branch on East 86th Street were smashed and pro-Palestinian messages were painted on its doors.
body: The NYPD Hate Crimes Task Force is investigating vandalism at a Capital One branch at 249 East 86th Street on the Upper East Side, where front windows were smashed and messages were painted on the doors Monday morning, amNY reported.

Officers from the 19th Precinct responded to a report at about 7:40 a.m. on Oct. 19 and found several windows broken, apparently with bricks, according to amNY. Other windows and the front doors were marked with red stenciled letters reading "PAL ACTION" and "DROP ELBIT."

ABC7 reported that the first phrase may refer to Palestine Action, a U.K.-based group, according to amNY. Elbit is an Israeli arms manufacturer, and pro-Palestinian protesters have previously targeted Capital One over lines of credit to the company.

City Council Speaker Julie Menin called the vandalism deeply disturbing and unacceptable, said she had been in contact with the NYPD and asked whether it could be an antisemitic hate crime, amNY reported. No injuries were reported.
No arrests have been made, and police have not released a description of a suspect. The investigation is ongoing, according to amNY.

sources.title: Vandalism attack at Upper East Side bank being investigated as possible hate crime: NYPD

stories.title: Woman Beaten and Robbed on Central Park's East Drive; Three Suspects Sought
stories.dek: Police say three people struck a 32-year-old woman near 90th Street and fled with her backpack on Sunday night.
body: A 32-year-old woman was beaten and robbed while walking on Central Park's East Drive near 90th Street on Sunday evening, Hoodline reported, citing police.

The attack happened at about 9:45 p.m., according to Hoodline. Police said three unidentified people struck the woman repeatedly in the head and fled with her backpack. PIX11 reported that the suspects were last seen heading toward Fifth Avenue.

EMS responded, but the woman refused medical attention, Hoodline reported. Police have not released descriptions of the suspects. The park, which is open daily from 6 a.m. to 1 a.m., is patrolled by the NYPD's Central Park Precinct.
Hoodline noted earlier incidents along East Drive, including four gunpoint robberies within about an hour on Sept. 17, in which three men on bicycles took cellphones, according to West Side Rag.
No arrests have been made, and the investigation is ongoing, according to Hoodline. Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Woman Beaten, Robbed on Central Park's East Drive, NYPD Hunts Three Suspects

stories.title: Robber Assaults 19-Year-Old Worker at Staten Island's Bricktown Centre
stories.dek: Police are seeking help identifying a shoplifting suspect who attacked an employee who confronted them at a store on Bricktown Way.
body: Police are asking for the public's help identifying a shoplifting suspect who attacked a 19-year-old employee inside a store at 165 Bricktown Way, at Bricktown Centre at Charleston on Staten Island, Hoodline reported, citing NYPD Crime Stoppers.

The attack happened at about 6:10 p.m. on a Sunday, according to Hoodline. Police said the suspect took merchandise and walked past all points of sale without paying. When the employee confronted the suspect, the suspect attacked her, and Hoodline reported that the attack included a sexual assault.

Accounts of the weapon differ. The article's text said the suspect struck the worker with what it described as a firearm, while the page's summary said she was pepper-sprayed. Hoodline did not reconcile the two accounts.
Police have not released a description of the suspect. Hoodline quoted no police officials directly.

No arrests had been announced as of the Crime Stoppers alert, and the suspect remains at large, according to Hoodline. A reward of up to $3,500 is offered for information leading to an arrest and felony indictment. Tips can be shared with Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Staten Island Robber Assaults Teen Worker at Bricktown Centre

stories.title: Contractor Pleads Guilty After 10 Drywall Workers Go Unpaid on UWS Job
stories.dek: KEP Construction LLC pleaded guilty to grand larceny and scheme to defraud over $67,275 in wages withheld from immigrant workers.
body: KEP Construction LLC pleaded guilty to grand larceny and scheme to defraud after prosecutors said it withheld $67,275 in pay from 10 drywall workers, Hoodline reported.

Prosecutors said the company received more than $1.3 million from a general contractor for work on several buildings, including a 23-story high-rise at 270 West 96th Street on the Upper West Side, according to Hoodline. The workers were owed for work done between September 2023 and February 2024, with individual amounts ranging from $2,600 to $11,000, according to court records cited from Upper West Side Patch.

Some workers received checks that bounced or no payment at all, Hoodline reported. All 10 were immigrants and non-native English speakers, according to court records. The investigation began after workers repeatedly texted the company's owner pleading for their wages.
The owner, Kendis Paul, was indicted in January 2025 and has pleaded not guilty, according to Hoodline. He is presumed innocent. The report did not include sentencing information for the company.

Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg announced that nearly $70,000 in wages had been returned to the workers, Hoodline reported. The Workers' Justice Project helped the workers file claims with the state Department of Labor, according to Documented NY.

sources.title: KEP Construction LLC Pleads Guilty After 10 Upper West Side Drywall Workers Go Unpaid

stories.title: Man, 54, Wounded in Shooting Outside Maria Hernandez Park
stories.dek: Police are seeking three people after a 54-year-old man was shot in the leg in front of 202 Starr Street in Bushwick.
body: A 54-year-old man was shot in the leg in front of 202 Starr Street in Bushwick on the afternoon of Oct. 8, Hoodline reported.

Uniformed NYPD officers who were in nearby Maria Hernandez Park on an unrelated matter heard the shots and reached the man within moments, according to a Grime Square report cited by Hoodline. He was taken to a hospital and listed in stable condition.

Police are seeking three unidentified people wanted for assault, according to an NYPD Crime Stoppers post. Police said one person brought a gun, a second displayed and fired it, and a third took the weapon. All three fled south on foot along Knickerbocker Avenue, Hoodline reported.

The 83rd Precinct, which covers Bushwick, has seen total crime rise 15% year over year through October, with felony assaults up 35.2%, according to Grime Square. Citywide, officials announced record-low shootings for the first nine months of the year.
No arrests had been made as of mid-October, according to Grime Square. Anyone with information can contact Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Bushwick Shooting Outside Maria Hernandez Park Leaves Man, 54, Wounded

stories.title: Dyker Heights Mother and Two Children Reported Missing
stories.dek: The NYPD is asking for help locating a 40-year-old woman who left her home with her two young children on Oct. 9.
body: The NYPD is asking the public for help finding a 40-year-old Dyker Heights woman and her two children, ages 5 and 9, who have been missing for more than a week, Hoodline reported.
Police cited by the New York Daily News said the woman left the family's home with both children at about 10:10 a.m. on Oct. 9, after an argument with her husband, according to Hoodline.

Police describe the woman as about 5 feet 8 inches tall and 135 pounds, with shoulder-length red hair and blue eyes, Hoodline reported. No description of the children was provided. The 68th Precinct patrols Dyker Heights.

Hoodline did not report whether an AMBER Alert had been issued. Under New York's AMBER plan, alerts require reasonable cause to believe a child was abducted or is in imminent danger; otherwise agencies can request a Missing Child Alert through the state's Missing Persons Clearinghouse, according to Hoodline.
As of the report, the three had not been found. Anyone with information is asked to contact NYPD Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Dyker Heights Mom, Two Kids Missing as NYPD Seeks Help

stories.title: NYPD Seeks Two Suspects in Lower Manhattan Robbery Pattern
stories.dek: Crime Stoppers released images of two people wanted in connection with a string of robberies in the 5th Precinct.
body: NYPD Crime Stoppers is asking the public to help identify two people wanted in connection with a pattern of robberies in Lower Manhattan's 5th Precinct, Hoodline reported.
The unit posted images of the pair on X on the night of Friday, Oct. 16, according to Hoodline. The 5th Precinct covers southeastern Manhattan, including Chinatown, Little Italy and the Bowery.

The NYPD has not said when or where the robberies occurred, what was taken or whether anyone was hurt, Hoodline reported. Police have not released names, ages or descriptions of the two people sought.

At an Oct. 6 briefing, the department said robberies were down 12% citywide this year, with about 1,400 fewer complaints than at the same point in 2025, according to Hoodline. Police did not say whether the 5th Precinct follows that trend. Hoodline noted other robbery patterns reported in the Bronx and Manhattan this year but said none had been linked to this case.
The two suspects remain unidentified. Crime Stoppers offers up to $3,500 for anonymous information leading to an arrest and indictment, and tips can be called in to 1-800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: NYPD Hunts Two Suspects in Lower Manhattan Robbery Pattern, Seeks Tips

stories.title: Canarsie Man, 67, Beaten From Behind and Robbed of Phone and iPad
stories.dek: An attacker punched and kicked a 67-year-old man near East 101st Street and Avenue J, then fled with his devices, police said.
body: A 67-year-old man was beaten and robbed on a Monday afternoon near East 101st Street and Avenue J in Canarsie, Hoodline reported, citing police.

The attacker approached the man from behind and punched and kicked him repeatedly as he tried to defend himself, according to Hoodline. The man suffered cuts and swelling to his face and was taken to Mount Sinai Brooklyn for treatment.
The attacker ran off along East 101st Street with the man's cellphone and iPad, Hoodline reported, citing News12 Brooklyn.

Police have not released a description of the attacker, and no arrest has been reported, according to Hoodline. The outlet noted earlier attacks on older men in the area, including a February assault on an 80-year-old on Rockaway Parkway, but said no link to this case has been established.
The investigation is ongoing, according to Hoodline. Anyone with information about the attack is asked to call NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS (8477).

sources.title: Canarsie Man, 67, Beaten From Behind, Robbed of Phone and iPad

stories.title: Williamsbridge Woman, 27, Has Phone Snatched From Pocket
stories.dek: Police are seeking a man who took a woman's cellphone from her back pocket near Capuchin Way and East Gun Hill Road in August.
body: Police are searching for a man who took a 27-year-old woman's cellphone from her back pocket near Capuchin Way and East Gun Hill Road in Williamsbridge, the Bronx, Hoodline reported.
The theft happened on Aug. 25, according to police, as cited by Hoodline. The man walked up behind the woman, grabbed the phone and fled on foot, News 12 New York reported.
Police described the suspect as a man last seen wearing a black tank top and black pants, according to Hoodline. The location is on a busy stretch of East Gun Hill Road near the Bx30 bus line.
The 47th Precinct is investigating, Hoodline reported. NYPD CompStat data through Oct. 11 show 618 grand larceny complaints in the precinct this year, down 22.6% from 798 at the same point in 2025.

The suspect remains at large, and no arrest has been reported. Hoodline did not explain why the August incident was being publicized in October. Anyone with information can call NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Williamsbridge Woman, 27, Has Phone Snatched From Pocket, NYPD Hunts Suspect

stories.title: Officer Struck by SUV on Loud-Music Call in Hunts Point; Driver at Large
stories.dek: An NYPD officer suffered a leg injury when a driver in a white Honda SUV struck him and fled, police said.
body: An NYPD officer responding to a loud-music complaint in Hunts Point was struck by a white Honda SUV whose driver fled, Hoodline reported, citing police.

The crash happened at about 7:20 p.m. Saturday at Garrison Avenue and Whittier Street, within the 41st Precinct, according to Hoodline. Several officers had responded to the complaint and found a large crowd. A person from the crowd drove off in the SUV and struck the officer, police said, as cited by News12 New York.
The officer suffered a leg injury and was taken by paramedics to Lincoln Hospital, according to Hoodline. Police said he is expected to recover. His name and age were not released.
Police said the driver sped away after the crash. No description of the driver was released, Hoodline reported.
No arrests had been announced as of Saturday night, and the investigation was ongoing, according to Hoodline. Anyone with information can contact NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS.

sources.title: Hunts Point Officer Hit By SUV During Loud Music Call, Driver Still At Large

stories.title: Indicted Deed-Theft Suspect Now Says Her Own Home Was Stolen
stories.dek: A Manhattan woman charged in the alleged theft of a dying Kew Gardens Hills widow's home has sued her co-defendant, claiming he took her Flushing house.
body: A 69-year-old Manhattan woman indicted in the alleged deed theft of a Kew Gardens Hills home now claims her co-defendant also stole her own property in Flushing, Hoodline reported.

Deepa V. Roy and Victor Quimis were indicted in August 2025, accused of forging the signature of an 88-year-old homeowner in hospice care in 2024 to transfer her house to themselves, according to Hoodline. The woman died in June 2025. Both have pleaded not guilty and are due back in court Nov. 4, and both are presumed innocent.

In a lawsuit filed Sept. 16 in Queens Supreme Court, first reported by the New York Post, Roy alleges Quimis took her Flushing house after her husband died in 2023, Hoodline reported. She says she had asked him to help remove squatters and that he created deeds making himself the owner. She seeks at least $1 million.

Roy's criminal attorney, Jeremy Saland, said she disputes the allegations and may herself have been a victim of Quimis, according to Hoodline. The late homeowner's son told the Post he believes Roy is trying to deflect blame. Quimis and his lawyers did not respond to requests for comment.

The Times reported that the case was the first indictment under New York's law treating deed theft as grand larceny. Complaints to the attorney general's office rose from 149 in 2023 to 517 in 2025, according to CBS News New York.

sources.title: Queens Deed-Theft Suspect Deepa Roy Now Says Her Own Home Was Stolen Too

stories.title: Man Shot Dead on Midtown Subway Platform; Masked Gunman Sought
stories.dek: A 26-year-old Bronx man was fatally shot during an argument at the 53rd Street-Seventh Avenue station, and police are searching for the suspect.
body: A 26-year-old Bronx man was shot and killed during an argument with another man at the 53rd Street-Seventh Avenue subway station in Midtown Manhattan on Saturday, FOX 5 NY reported. Police said the attack was not random.

The shooting happened just before 12:30 p.m., according to FOX 5. Officials said the argument began on the northbound platform, continued as the two men boarded a subway car and resumed after they returned to the platform, when the suspect drew a gun and shot the man in the chest.
First responders took the man to a hospital, where he was pronounced dead, FOX 5 reported.
The NYPD released surveillance images of the suspect, a man wearing a red tracksuit, a black vest, a black face mask and a black backpack, according to FOX 5. His name and whereabouts are unknown.
The search for the suspect is ongoing. Anyone with information can call NYPD Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS, or 1-888-57-PISTA for Spanish.

sources.title: NYPD manhunt after deadly shooting at Midtown Manhattan subway station

stories.title: Astoria Man, 42, Shot in Leg on Steinway Street
stories.dek: A gunman opened fire near Steinway Street and 31st Avenue early Saturday, and witnesses reported seeing a white SUV drive away.
body: A 42-year-old man was shot in the left leg early Saturday on Steinway Street near 31st Avenue in Astoria, Hoodline reported.

The shooting happened at about 6:36 a.m. on Oct. 17 near a sidewalk bench, according to Hoodline. The gunman fled, and witnesses told investigators they saw a white SUV driving away. No description of a suspect was released.

Responding officers drove the man to Elmhurst Hospital in their patrol car rather than waiting for an ambulance, the New York Daily News reported, as cited by Hoodline. Police said he was expected to survive.

Detectives interviewed witnesses at the scene and were canvassing for surveillance footage of the gunman or the SUV, according to Hoodline. Neighbors suggested a link to a nearby party venue, which police have not confirmed, and police have not disclosed a motive.
There were no arrests as of Saturday. Police have not indicated any connection to a fatal shooting on Steinway Street in September, Hoodline reported.

sources.title: Astoria Man, 42, Shot in Leg as Gunfire Erupts on Steinway Street

stories.title: Five Men Sought After Man Stabbed Outside University Avenue Building
stories.dek: A 35-year-old man was stabbed in the back and cut on the hand outside 2274 University Ave. in the Bronx and is expected to recover.
body: Police are looking for at least five men after a 35-year-old man was stabbed outside a residential building in University Heights, the Bronx, late Thursday night, Hoodline reported, citing police sources.

The attack happened in front of 2274 University Avenue, according to Hoodline. Officers found the man with a stab wound to his back and a cut to his left hand, News12 Bronx reported, as cited by Hoodline.
EMS took the man to St. Barnabas Hospital, and he is expected to recover, according to Hoodline.

Police sources said they are searching for at least five men believed to be connected to the attack. The circumstances that led to the stabbing have not been disclosed, and no descriptions of the men were released, Hoodline reported.

No arrests have been made, and the investigation is ongoing. Anyone with information can call Crime Stoppers at 1-800-577-TIPS; the program offers rewards of up to $3,500 for tips leading to an arrest and indictment, according to Hoodline.

sources.title: Five Men Sought After Stabbing Leaves Bronx Man Wounded in University Heights

stories.title: South Richmond Hill Mother Charged With Murder in Death of Daughter, 5
stories.dek: A 32-year-old woman was held without bail after prosecutors charged her in the death of her kindergarten-age daughter at their Queens home.
body: A 32-year-old South Richmond Hill woman has been charged with murder in the death of her 5-year-old daughter and is being held without bail, QNS reported, citing the Queens District Attorney's Office.

Officers from the 102nd Precinct responded to a 911 call reporting an assault at the family's home on 110th Street shortly before 7 p.m. on Oct. 14, according to QNS. The girl was taken to Jamaica Hospital Medical Center, where she was pronounced dead.

The woman was taken into custody as a person of interest the next day and was charged at Jamaica Hospital, where she was undergoing a psychiatric evaluation, QNS reported. The criminal complaint cites witness information, statements attributed to her and an autopsy finding that QNS said was consistent with asphyxia.

At her arraignment Friday before Queens Criminal Court Judge Jennifer Saint-Preux, the woman did not enter a plea, according to QNS. She is due back in court Oct. 20. A relative told reporters she had psychological issues, had recently been hospitalized and had stopped taking her medication.
The charges are allegations, and the woman is presumed innocent. The case is ongoing.

sources.title: South Richmond Hill mother held without bail after she was charged with murder for causing the death of her young daughter: DA

stories.title: Suspicious Powder Mailed to Rep. Ritchie Torres' Bronx Office
stories.dek: Six people were reportedly exposed to a substance later found to be non-hazardous, and the FBI is investigating.
body: An envelope containing a suspicious powder prompted a hazardous materials response at U.S. Rep. Ritchie Torres' district office on East Fordham Road in the Bronx on Friday afternoon, amNY reported.

The FDNY received a call at 1:23 p.m. on Oct. 16 about the powder at 540 East Fordham Road and sent hazmat units, according to amNY. The department said six people were reportedly exposed. A spokesperson said the substance was determined to be non-hazardous and no injuries were reported.

Torres said his staff immediately notified the FBI, NYPD and FDNY, and the envelope was turned over to the FBI, amNY reported. In a post on X, he said his team was shaken but would not be deterred, and he described threats against elected officials and their staff as a new normal.

The incident came a day after suspicious mail was sent to the New York offices of Sens. Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand, according to amNY. The FBI said it and the Postal Inspection Service are investigating suspicious mailings sent nationwide, some containing an unknown substance.
The FBI declined to confirm whether the Torres envelope was part of that series. The investigation is ongoing.

sources.title: Suspicious powder sent to Rep. Ritchie Torres' Bronx office in latest mail scare targeting New York Democratic pols

stories.title: Woman Sought in Slashing at 145th Street Subway Station
stories.dek: Transit detectives released images of a woman accused of cutting a 21-year-old passenger's arm during an argument in Harlem.
body: Transit detectives are searching for a woman who slashed a 21-year-old woman's arm during an argument at the 145th Street station on the 2 line in Harlem, amNY reported, citing the NYPD.

The attack happened at about 8 p.m. on Sept. 11 in the station mezzanine, according to amNY. Police said the suspect confronted the victim and started a verbal dispute for undisclosed reasons. It escalated into a physical fight, and the suspect pulled out a sharp object and cut the victim's arm.
EMS took the victim to Mount Sinai Hospital in stable condition, amNY reported. The suspect fled on foot in an unknown direction.

Police described the suspect as a woman wearing a black shirt, black pants and black sneakers and carrying a black bag. The NYPD released images of her on Wednesday night, according to amNY. The case was reported to the 32nd Precinct and Transit District 3.
The suspect remained at large as of publication. Anyone with information can call Crime Stoppers at 800-577-TIPS or 888-57-PISTA for Spanish.

sources.title: Harlem subway slasher sought for slicing woman's arm during argument
